title: 6.11.8 Lab: A settings screen that remembers
description: A sound options screen: up and down step the level, M mutes, and both are saved with storeItem when they change and loaded with getItem when the game starts, so the game remembers them.

steps.title: Change the level and the mute
steps.instructions:
The starter is your 6.11.7 game with a fifth screen, `'settings'`: O on the title opens it, and O there goes back. The orange basket stays at the bottom of every screen, this one too: a sprite is drawn on every frame until the sketch removes it, and this game keeps it. That is expected. It shows `level` (how loud everything is, 0 to 10) and whether the sound is on. Two variables hold them, `let level = 5;` and `let muted = false;`, and `applySound()` turns them into sound for everything at once with `masterVolume(muted ? 0 : level / 10);` (6.11.6). `soundChanged()` calls `applySound()` and plays the chime as a sample, so the player hears the new level.

This `level` is not the one from 6.11.4. There it was the tune's own volume, and M flipped `masterVolume()` between 0 and 1 itself. Here `level` is how loud everything is, and only `applySound()` sets `masterVolume`, from `level` and `muted`. So 6.11.4's M would undo itself here: `soundChanged()` runs `applySound()` on the same press and sets the volume straight back. Here M flips `muted`, and `applySound()` does the rest.

`settingsScreen()` runs every frame on that screen and so far has only the O key. Above that line, add the controls: up raises `level` by 1 (only while it is below 10), down lowers it by 1 (only while it is above 0), and M flips `muted` with `muted = !muted;`. Each one then calls `soundChanged();`. Use `kb.presses`, so one press is one step (6.3.3). Run it, click the canvas, press O, and try them.
hints: `if (kb.presses('up') && level < 10) { level += 1; soundChanged(); }`, then the same shape for down and for M.
`!muted` is the opposite of `muted`: `true` becomes `false`, and `false` becomes `true`.

steps.title: Save each change
hints: Saving in `draw()` would write 60 times a second a value that changes only when a key is pressed.

steps.title: Load them when the game starts
hints: Two `getItem`s, each followed by an `if (... !== null)`.
On the very first run both give back `null`, so `level` stays 5 and `muted` stays false.

requirements.title: Up and down change the level
requirements.description: Under kb.presses, one key raises level by 1 and another lowers it, and level is what masterVolume uses (through applySound). Any variable name works. Help: 6.3.3 (Reading: moSHion docs: Input edges)
requirements.hint: if (kb.presses('up') && level < 10) { level += 1; soundChanged(); }, and the same for 'down'.

requirements.title: M flips the sound off and on
requirements.description: Under a kb.presses test, muted is flipped (muted = !muted, or an if and an else). Setting masterVolume under the key, the way 6.11.4 did, does not count here: soundChanged() calls applySound(), which sets it straight back from level and muted. Help: 6.11.6 (Reading: Music that follows the game)

requirements.title: A change is saved
requirements.description: storeItem runs when a key changes a setting: inside that if, or in a function it calls, such as soundChanged(). What it saves is the setting itself (level, muted), not a fixed value such as 5. Help: 6.5.3 (Reading: storeItem: Save Game Data)
requirements.hint: storeItem('soundLevel', level); and storeItem('soundMuted', muted); at the end of soundChanged().

requirements.title: The settings are loaded at the start
requirements.description: setup() (or loadSettings(), which it calls) reads a setting with getItem, keeps what comes back (in a variable, or straight into level), and deals with the null that comes back when nothing was saved: !== null, === null, ?? or ||. Help: 6.5.5 (Reading: getItem: Load Saved Data)
requirements.hint: const savedLevel = getItem('soundLevel'); then if (savedLevel !== null) level = savedLevel;
